name: Luca — good hands, bad reasons
summary: Around 150 hours, flying weekly, genuinely capable in the air and has done a manoeuvres course. But everyone he flies with is on a C, he's chasing them, he expects the new wing to handle turbulence better than his does, he launches on days he isn't sure about, and he's had a few near misses he can't explain.
why_this_persona: The strong-skills/poor-motivation case the brief asks for. Tests that the psychological half can decide the result on its own, that a manoeuvres course cannot buy the result back, and — importantly — that the 'equipment_as_a_fix_with_thin_readiness' combination gate correctly does NOT fire for a pilot whose readiness is genuinely not thin. The cap comes from the Not yet psychological floor instead.

notes: Computed skills 84.8, psychological 25.2, total 56.2 plus a 2-point manoeuvre bonus = 58.2. The psychological floor of 35 produces Not yet regardless of the total.

Negative check — SIV cannot buy a result. He has done one manoeuvres course, which is worth exactly 2 points on the total and nothing at all to the category floors, so it must not change his band. knowledge/disagreements.md point 1: a small positive signal, never a cap and never a rescue.

Gate check — 'equipment_as_a_fix_with_thin_readiness' must NOT fire. His motive and expectation both match the first clause, but the second clause requires thin readiness (skills below 62, or frozen hands, or a frozen collapse) and he has none of those. This is deliberate per knowledge/disagreements.md point 9: a comparison-driven motive on its own is not enough to cap a result. The psychological floor is the mechanism that catches him, and it catches him on the whole pattern rather than one answer.

Gate check — 'ambition_without_readiness' must NOT fire either, for the same reason: his ambitions are on the gate's list but his skills score is 84.8, far above the 55 trigger. Ambition alone is never penalised.

Reviewer tone check: the 'not_yet_category_floor:psychological' message must name the question areas without quoting his answers back at him, and must not read as a character assessment. 'None of that is a judgement on you as a pilot' is load-bearing per docs/design-context.md.
